arguments.concept: Use the length equivalences $10$ mm $=1$ cm, $100$ cm $=1$ m and $1000$ m $=1$ km. Converting to smaller units multiplies the numerical value; converting to larger units divides it. Choose the factor linking the stated source and target units and keep the value exact.

worked_example.problem: Convert $8.4$ cm to millimetres. Give the numerical value.

arguments.concept: For adjacent listed mass units, $1000$ mg $=1$ g, $1000$ g $=1$ kg and $1000$ kg $=1$ t. Capacity uses $1000$ ml $=1$ l. Multiply by $1000$ when moving to the smaller unit and divide by $1000$ when moving to the larger unit.

steps: There are $1000$ grams in one kilogram, so divide by $1000$.

arguments.concept: Chain compatible conversion factors until the target unit is reached. For mixed-unit totals, differences or counts, first convert the quantities to a common unit, then perform the requested operation. Keep exact decimal values throughout.

Write conversion factors as ratios of equal quantities and orient them so unwanted units cancel. A contextual rate, such as cost per metre or grams per second, similarly links the named quantities. Multiply the numerical factors after checking that only the requested unit remains.

steps: Use the conversion factor $60\text{ min}/1\text{ h}$.
Multiply: $(4.25\text{ h})(60\text{ min}/1\text{ h})$. The hours cancel.

arguments.concept: A rate is a quotient of units. Convert its numerator and denominator using factors oriented to cancel the original units. Since $1$ km $=1000$ m and $1$ h $=3600$ s, divide km/h by $3.6$ to obtain m/s, or multiply m/s by $3.6$ to obtain km/h. A rate per second becomes a rate per hour by multiplying by $3600$.

steps: Use the factors $1000\text{ m}/1\text{ km}$ and $1\text{ h}/3600\text{ s}$.
The remaining units are m/s, with value $108\cdot1000/3600=30$.

arguments.concept: An area conversion squares the length conversion factor, and a volume conversion cubes it. Thus $1$ m² $=10000$ cm². For capacity, $1$ l $=1000$ cm³ and $1$ m³ $=1000$ l. If dimensions are given, calculate the area or volume first, then convert its units.
